basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 9:2 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 131. Cur [enim] homo in terrorem caeteris animantibus positus est (Gen. IX, 2)?--'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 131. Cur [enim] homo in terrorem caeteris animantibus positus est (Gen. IX, 2)?-- Resp. In solatium transactae vindictae, et ne pauci homines a pluribus opprimerentur bestiis; et ut scirent se irrationabilibus dominari debere, non rationabilibus. Unde et primi patres nostri pastores pecorum, non reges hominum fuisse leguntur.
